_note: The body (2026-11-13, rebuilt on a professional's figures; ADR-052 note: derived, never adjusted). Top speed: top_speed_min + (top_speed_max - top_speed_min) x max_speed. Acceleration: (accel_min + (accel_max - accel_min) x explosive_force) x weight_ref / weight, dimmed by fatigue (ADR-030: 1 - fatigue_coefficient x fatigue, floored). Braking: decel_min + (decel_max - decel_min) x body_control: he slows down to stop where he is going, and to turn. He moves in a straight line towards his target (before, a diagonal ran 1.4 times his top speed). His pace is his: when he contests something (pressing, going in, going for the ball, running in behind, carrying it) he runs as fast as he can; when he takes up his place he goes at the speed that gets him there in about reposition_ticks. Before, every player ran every run at full speed (13 km a match, a third of the time above 4 m/s). The characteristics are read through the range, never to zero (before, an average player reached 4.5 m/s, accelerating at 1.5 m/s2). With the ball (2026-11-13, plan L0-CLOSE 10a): his top speed is with_ball_share_min + (with_ball_share_max - with_ball_share_min) x dribbling of his sprint: the good dribbler runs almost as fast with it. Work rate (2026-11-13, plan L0-CLOSE 10c): without the ball, out of a contest, he gives work_rate_floor + (1 - work_rate_floor) x work_rate of the pace his side needs. Turning (2026-11-13, plan L0-CLOSE 10e): changing direction by more than 60 degrees he brakes and turns with turn_share_min + (turn_share_max - turn_share_min) x joint_mobility of his braking: the stiff player needs longer to turn. The touch (2026-11-13, plan L0-CLOSE 11): running with the ball he plays it ahead and meets it again a few steps later; between two touches it rolls on its own, slowed by the ground (ball.json). He touches it every 1 + (touch_steps_max - 1) x (his speed / top_speed_max) x (1 - dribbling) steps, at step_hz steps a second: walking, or the best dribbler, every step; the worst dribbler at full speed every touch_steps_max. The touch is weighed so that the ball comes back to his foot after that many steps at his pace; how far ahead it goes follows from the ground friction, nothing else.
_source: Acceleration (SIM 194): the in-situ acceleration-speed profile of professional players on match days, Alonso-Callejo, Garcia-Unanue, Perez-Guerra, Gomez, Sanchez-Sanchez, Gallardo, Oliva-Lozano and Felipe 2022 (Scientific Reports 12:19266, doi 10.1038/s41598-022-23790-w; 25 players of a Spanish second-division club, GPS at 18 Hz): the theoretical maximal acceleration A0 is 8.26-8.68 m/s2 by position (SD 0.36-0.81), the theoretical maximal speed S0 9.22-9.50 m/s, and the acceleration falls linearly from A0 at rest to zero at S0. accel_min and accel_max are the pooled mean (about 8.4) less and plus two standard deviations (about 0.6): 7.2 and 9.6 m/s2, the acceleration from rest; as he speeds up it falls by the share of his top speed he has reached. Before, 2.5-5 m/s2 applied whatever his speed, read from Harper, Carling and Kiely 2019, whose figures are the thresholds that count a match effort as an acceleration, not what a player can do. Professional footballers' peak sprint speeds of about 7.5-10 m/s (27-36 km/h, top-league tracking data); maximal accelerations of about 2.5-5 m/s2 and decelerations larger than accelerations, up to 5-6 m/s2 and more (Harper, Carling and Kiely 2019, Sports Medicine 49:1923-1947). weight_ref and height_ref: median professional (78 kg, 180 cm). reposition_ticks (3 s), fatigue_coefficient and fatigue_floor: arbitrary, declared, to be sourced at L3. with_ball_share_min and _max (75-95% of the sprint with the ball): order of magnitude, declared, to be sourced at L3. work_rate_floor: arbitrary, declared. turn_share_min and _max: arbitrary, declared, to be sourced at L3 (change-of-direction tests). step_hz: order of magnitude of a running cadence (about 3-5 steps a second from jogging to sprinting), declared, to be sourced at L3. touch_steps_max: arbitrary, declared (a player knocking the ball on at a sprint touches it every few strides), to be sourced at L3 (dribbling tracking data).
